content.content:
**The four agents**
- **Producer:** Preps the session and helps you run it. Per the page, it prepares your questions, script, and studio so you're ready to record.
- **Editor:** Turns your raw recording into a finished episode. It can also suggest edits and tell you what would take the episode further.
- **Clipper:** Finds your best moments and cuts them for social. It can also pull clips from old recordings.
- **Marketer:** Writes captions and schedules posts. It drafts posts, captions, and newsletters.

**Editor operations (listed on the page)**
- **Cuts:** Tightens pacing and cuts preamble, for example removing 21 seconds of intro in the demo.
- **Filler words and pauses:** Cuts filler words and removes pauses.
- **Layouts:** Switches layouts.
- **Captions:** Adds captions and your branding.
- **Audio:** Cleans up audio.
- **Rough cuts:** Builds rough cuts for review.
- **B-roll and motion graphics:** Suggests them. The page doesn't say the Editor inserts them directly.

You have the final say on every change, and you can keep any step manual.

**Plans and pricing**
- Agents are available on every Riverside plan.
- You can try Riverside free for 14 days.
- Agent capabilities depend on your plan.
- Features that use AI credits, such as video enhancement, consume credits when an agent applies them.
- The page gives no specific prices.

**Platforms**
- Web and mobile. The page says everything the agents do on web they also do on mobile.
- The navigation also links to a Mac app.

**MCP and memory**
- **MCP:** The page links to an MCP page in its navigation but doesn't describe it.
- **Memory:** The page doesn't mention memory.

**Screen Studio 4 features** (no release date shown; the page is copyright 2026 and says "Available now")

**Video and zoom**
- **Glass Loupe:** magnifies a detail through a curved glass lens. Not labeled beta. Uses an upscaler that runs on your Mac (on-device).
- **Sharper zooms:** upscales your recording wherever a zoom enlarges it. Runs on your Mac's graphics chip (on-device).
- **Auto zoom:** the page doesn't describe this as a named feature. It only mentions that zooms start animating early and that Screen Studio 3 zooms may show a different part of the recording.
- **Exports:** up to 3x faster on Apple silicon. Pricing lists up to 4K at 60 fps. No on-device/cloud note.

**Camera**
- **Camera cutout:** labeled **beta**. Removes your background on your Mac (on-device).
- **Split screen:** side by side, or stacked in vertical video. No beta label or on-device/cloud note.
- **Face tracking:** keeps your face centered. No beta label or note.
- **Color grading:** 12 presets, adjustable strength, or your own LUT file. No beta label or note.
- **LUTs:** load your own LUT file for the webcam. No beta label or note.
- **Camera crop, Hide during silence:** no beta label or note.

**Audio**
- **Noise reduction:** reduces background noise and room echo. Your voice is processed on your Mac (on-device). Requires Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later.
- **Podcast:** labeled **beta**. Makes your voice sound closer and fuller. Processed on your Mac (on-device). Requires Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later.

**Transcript and captions**
- **Cloud transcription:** uploads your microphone audio to create a transcript. Cloud, not on-device. Requires macOS 26 or later and a Screen Studio account.
- **Edit by transcript:** delete words in the transcript to cut them from the video. No beta label. The page doesn't say where editing runs.
- **Filler words and pauses:** finds "um," "uh," and long pauses. Requires a transcript made with Cloud transcription.
- **Captions:** style, color, and position options; line-by-line or word-by-word display; word animations. No beta label. The page doesn't say whether caption generation is on-device, though transcription requires Cloud transcription.

**Other new features**
- Ripple click effect (redrawn)
- Smaller recordings (up to 2x smaller)
- Preview toolbar for zooms, camera layouts, and masks
- Open where you left off
- Keyboard keycaps and cursor fade while typing
- Unsplash backgrounds (requires account; uses online search)
- Mask sensitive data
- Less color banding
- **Share project: labeled beta.** Requires a Screen Studio account. The page doesn't state on-device or cloud handling.
- Backup on every save, Trash removal, quit confirmation, and muted silent recordings

**Price**
- Yearly: $9/mo (save 69%)
- Monthly: $29/mo
- Every plan includes all features.
- Students and educators get 40% off.

Here is what the page does say about plans:

- **Free plan:** Available to start with, and upgrading unlocks "powerful features."
- **AI credits:** Each plan includes a set amount of credits monthly or yearly. Unused credits don't carry over, and the allowance refreshes on renewal. You can move to a higher credit allowance by upgrading.
- **Subtitles:** All paid plans include unlimited subtitle generation, with a fair use limit of 50 hours per month. Subtitle styles depend on plan, with more advanced styles on higher tiers.
- **Translations:** Minute-based and counted against your plan's allowance. Unused minutes don't roll over.
- **Pricing model:** Plans are charged per seat, so the price is multiplied by the number of editors. You're charged when you invite users.
- **Payments:** Prices appear in your local currency when available, otherwise in USD. Cards, PayPal, and Google or Apple Pay are accepted in some countries.
- **Enterprise:** A free trial is available for enterprise customers with at least 3 users, through Contact Sales.
- **Education:** Bespoke plans for faculty-wide use, through a sales form.
- **Cancellation:** You can turn off auto-renewal in your dashboard and keep premium access until the billing cycle ends.

content.content:
**HyperFrames** is an open-source framework from HeyGen that turns HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Its tagline is "Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents."

- **What it renders:** You write a composition as HTML with data attributes for timing and tracks. Animation can come from GSAP, CSS, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, WAAPI, or a custom adapter. The renderer seeks each frame in headless Chrome and encodes it with FFmpeg, so the same input produces the same video.
- **License:** Apache 2.0, with no per-render fees or commercial-use thresholds.
- **Agent skills:** The project ships 7 skills. The core set covers `/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, and `/media-use`. Three more install on demand: `/figma`, `/slideshow`, and `/remotion-to-hyperframes`. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and other agents. Installation is via the `hyperframes` CLI or a Claude Code plugin.
- **Stars:** About 76.6k stars and 7.0k forks, with 191 watchers at the time of the snapshot.
- **Latest release and dates:** The page doesn't show a version number or release dates. The Releases section is empty, so I can't confirm the latest release from this content.

**Pricing (old vs. new)**
- Pro now costs $19.99/month or $179.99/year. The annual plan rose from roughly $78 in February 2026, a change Newsweek reported on February 17, 2026. The page doesn't give the old monthly price.
- Standard ($9.99/month, mobile-only) removes the watermark and unlocks 1080p. Pro adds 4K and 8K.
- The Team plan starts near $24.99 per seat.

**Feature paywalling**
- The free tier lost its 1GB of cloud storage in August 2024, so free accounts can no longer sync projects across devices. Pro includes about 1TB.
- EditPilot, an AI editing agent, is bundled into Pro. The page says it's aimed at "webinars, interviews and product demos" rather than short social clips.

**Credits**
- Paid subscribers reach some underlying models, including Seedance 2.5, through "per-second credit billing" instead of a flat monthly cap.

**Creator reaction**
- The page cites Newsweek's coverage of the price jump, but it doesn't quote individual creators.
- CapCut and ByteDance did not publicly explain the price change.
- The author argues the free tier got worse even though its price didn't change, and points to alternatives like Meta's Edits, Veed, and Filmora.
- Most of the sentiment in the piece is the author's own assessment, not documented user feedback.

The AI can pick the best takes, add music and transitions, insert text overlays, and remove pauses in speech. It can also suggest edits based on the conversation. Creators can switch to the editing timeline to adjust things manually. YouTube describes it as "a collaborative partner that edits with you, not for you."

- **Timing:** Early 2027.
- **Models:** The article doesn't say which AI models power the tool.
- **Pricing:** The article doesn't mention pricing.

Listed features include AI Curation, Auto Reframe, AI Virality Score, AI Co-Pilot, Clip Anything, AI B-Roll, Team Workspace, Autopost & Scheduler, and Export to XML. The page claims it can create 30 clips in 10 minutes and save 90% of editing time.

**AI Producer (open beta):** A LinkedIn promo says it is "now available in Open Beta" and offers a free trial. It edits raw talking-head footage through chat, adding captions, b-roll, motion graphics, and sound effects. The page says it is not a template-based caption-and-reframe editor.

**Agent Opus:** The page contains only logo and brand asset files for this product. It gives no description, status, or features.

**Users and revenue:**
- The page states OpusClip supports over 16 million creators and businesses.
- No revenue figures are given.

input.prompt: List the AI features of DaVinci Resolve 21/21.1 (IntelliSearch, IntelliScript, AI assistant integration/MCP, Smart Reframe, AI audio, multicam, CineFocus, etc.) and which are Studio-only. Any mention of Claude/ChatGPT or MCP.

toolu_01Xz9ayxUdYsxcKr7GhLDnhX.prompt: List the AI features of DaVinci Resolve 21/21.1 (IntelliSearch, IntelliScript, AI assistant integration/MCP, Smart Reframe, AI audio, multicam, CineFocus, etc.) and which are Studio-only. Any mention of Claude/ChatGPT or MCP.

content.content:
**AI features in DaVinci Resolve 21/21.1 (per the page)**

- **AI IntelliSearch:** Finds people, objects, faces, or keywords in dialog. Results appear as whole clips in the Media Pool. The Photo page also uses it for plain-language photo search.
- **Advanced AI Speech Generator:** Creates speech from text using a Blackmagic voice model or a voice sampled from your own clip.
- **AI CineFocus:** Sets the focus point and depth of field, with optional keyframing for rack focus.
- **AI Face Age Transformer:** Adjusts an actor's apparent age.
- **AI Face Reshaper:** Changes facial feature shapes on tracked subjects.
- **AI Blemish Removal:** Reduces skin imperfections.
- **AI Slate ID:** Reads clapperboard metadata from the frame.
- **AI UltraSharpen:** Sharpens footage, including upscaled video and still photos.
- **AI Motion Deblur:** Reduces motion blur by rendering a new file.
- **AI Magic Mask (Photo page):** Makes one-click selections of people or objects.
- **DaVinci Neural Engine:** Powers many of these tools. The page says it is supported on Apple M series and Snapdragon X Elite.

**Studio-only**

The page ties only one AI capability to Studio: the Studio product "adds DaVinci Neural Engine for automatic AI region tracking." It does not label the other AI features as Free or Studio-only, so their availability can't be determined from this page.

**Not covered by the page**

- **Smart Reframe:** Mentioned only as a companion to vertical resolution settings, with no description.
- **Multicam:** The Replay Editor is described for multi-cam editing, but the page mentions no AI for it.
- **Claude, ChatGPT, or MCP:** The page doesn't mention any of them, and it doesn't mention AI assistant integration.

input.prompt: What is Prequel (the product behind this blog): platform, features, pricing model; and what does the post say Screen Studio 4 added and costs? Date.

toolu_01MoHG2ohgdu3FwuopdwFFAg.prompt: What is Prequel (the product behind this blog): platform, features, pricing model; and what does the post say Screen Studio 4 added and costs? Date.

content.content:
**ScreenKite** is a native macOS screen recorder and editor, with a Windows Beta. The post is dated October 1, 2026, and was written by the founder, Mike Chong, so its claims are promotional and unverified.

- **Platform:** It runs on macOS 15 or later, on both Apple Silicon and Intel. The post describes it as "Made in Swift for macOS." It also ships a native Windows Beta.
- **Recording:** You capture a display, window, or area, and the take opens on the timeline.
- **Editing:** It has a multi-track timeline with separate tracks for screen, camera, audio, music, overlays, captions, and zooms. You can cut by deleting words in the transcript, and it offers auto zoom, backgrounds, device frames, and captions with word-by-word highlighting.
- **Agent integration:** Coding agents, including Claude Code, ChatGPT Codex, Antigravity, Grok Build, and Kimi, can edit projects through 83 local editing tools. The post says the agent bills to the user's existing plan, and ScreenKite charges no AI fee. Risky edits return a plan first and apply only on a second call.
- **Pricing:** It is free to start, with unlimited recording and all editing features. Free exports carry a watermark and brand outro. A one-time $79.99 payment removes them, covers 3 devices, and never renews. The founder price lasts until October 31, 2026, then rises to $99.99. A 14-day refund is offered.
- **Open source:** The post does not say whether ScreenKite is open source. It describes a proprietary, paid one-time license with a free tier.

**Prequel** is a Mac screen recorder that automates editing. It adds zooms on clicks, frames your camera, and can place a background behind you. It runs on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 14 or later and exports up to 4K at 120 fps. Its features include a loupe, typing and click sounds, per-clip filters, titles, a teleprompter, speed control per clip, video import with captions, and shared links with chapters. Pricing is $9 a month or $39 once for a lifetime licence, with a 7-day trial that has no watermark.

**Screen Studio 4** was released on **2 October 2026**. According to the post, it added:
- A glass loupe
- A camera cutout (in beta)
- Face tracking and hide-during-silence
- Colour grading with twelve looks and LUT support
- Editing by transcript
- Split-screen layouts
- Sharper zoomed-in text
- Faster exports and smaller recordings

Its cost is $29 a month, or $9 a month billed yearly ($108 up front). There is no free tier, and the one-time licence was withdrawn in October 2025. Export still tops out at 4K and 60 fps.

The post is published by Prequel, so its comparisons come from a competitor.

input.segment: Creator-first video editors and AI repurposing tools as of 1 November 2026. This covers the mass-market editors (CapCut, Canva, Edits, YouTube Create, Premiere mobile), the AI editors built around a transcript or an agent (Descript, Riverside, Kapwing, VEED, Captions/Mirage), the short-form clip makers (OpusClip, Submagic), the screencast editors (Screen Studio 4, ScreenKite), the AI rough-cut assistants that hand off to a pro editor (Gling, Eddie AI, Selects), the pro editors as they chase creators (Final Cut Pro 12 / Apple Creator Studio, DaVinci Resolve 21.1), and the agent-written video frameworks (VEED OpenEdit, HeyGen HyperFrames). Pricing is given in one phrase in each tool's positioning field. Status is "shipped", "beta" or "announced", taken from the vendor's own wording where it gives one. Most of the 2026 detail comes from vendor changelogs fetched on 2026-11-01: Descript's Canny changelog, Riverside's product-updates page, VEED's changelog, Kapwing's monthly release notes, Submagic's Canny changelog, CapCut's newsroom, and Apple's Final Cut Pro release notes. A claim that rests only on third-party coverage is marked as such.

tools.name: CapCut (desktop, web, mobile; Standard / Pro / Ultra)
tools.positioning: The default mass-market editor (660M+ users in 170+ markets), now also ByteDance's AI generation front end (Seedance video, Seedream images, Seed Audio) with an agent layer arriving. In the US it runs under the TikTok USDS joint venture, closed 2026-01-22. Pricing: free core, then Pro at $19.99/mo or $179.99/yr (the annual price was about $78 before Feb 2026) with about 1,200 AI credits, Standard at $9.99 (mobile, regional) and Ultra at about $79/mo (third-party price trackers, Oct 2026).
tools.why_creators_pick_it: It is free or cheap on phone, desktop and web, with a huge template, effects and sound library tied to TikTok trends (400,000+ new templates a day), auto captions, and fast results. Most short-form creators already know it.

headline_features.detail: An assistant inside the multi-track editor. You describe an edit and it removes filler words, rough-trims talking heads, writes captions (bilingual where supported), emphasises key lines, reduces noise, enhances the voice and normalises loudness. English first. CapCut says it is not a one-click video maker and that you review its changes on the timeline. The Oct 2026 update adds prompt edits such as recolouring one object in a shot. A third party (hokai.io) says it is bundled into Pro.

headline_features.feature: Agentic creation, ChatGPT plugin, Skills Marketplace
headline_features.detail: An agent that turns a creative goal into a first draft on desktop, web and mobile, piloting 'in the coming months'. CapCut inside ChatGPT, also 'in the coming months'. A web marketplace for sharing reusable creative workflows ('Skills'). An AI-provenance checker is in pilot.

Smart Search (find clips by objects, speech, people and places), Auto Captions, Remove Filler Words, Scene Detection, Auto Cutout (background removal), chroma key, keyframes and graphs, colour grading (LUTs, wheels, skin-tone protection), selfie retouching with face tracking, Script to Video and text-to-speech.
Auto Reframe (subject-aware aspect-ratio change) moved from a free preview to Pro on desktop, web and mobile. Basic crop and zoom stay free.

headline_features.feature: Generative studios: Video Studio, Director Mode, Design Studio
headline_features.detail: Seedance interactive editing changes one timestamp, character or element without regenerating the scene. Director Mode takes an AI short drama from script to characters to shots to assembled edit; it is on CapCut Web globally, with the US rollout 'coming soon'. Design Studio has an infinite canvas and Skills. CapCut reports 6B+ AI outputs in 2026 and 7M+ creators using its AI features daily.
headline_features.status: shipped (Director Mode: not yet in the US)

tools.name: Descript
tools.positioning: Editing video by editing its transcript, now led by Underlord, an agentic co-editor that offers a choice of models, plus recording (Rooms), publishing and an API with an MCP server. Aimed at podcasters, YouTubers, educators and marketing teams. Pricing: free plan, then Hobbyist $24 ($16 annual), Creator $35 ($24) and Business $65 ($50) per seat, metered by media hours plus AI credits (third-party summary, checked against Descript's pricing on 2026-08-20).
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Cutting a talk by deleting words is the fastest edit there is, and Studio Sound, Eye Contact, filler removal and AI voice fixes come in one place. Underlord does the first pass. It works well for podcasts and talking-head YouTube.

headline_features.detail: Underlord v2 (Jan 2026) used about 20% fewer credits for a full edit. It lets you pick the model (Claude, Gemini, GPT; Claude Opus 5.5 is the Enterprise default). Each editing turn now gets an automatic review pass (May 2026), and since Oct 2026 Underlord states its plans in plain language. It previews audio and video before applying (Mar 2026). It has a Revert button, an @ context picker and per-project chat history.

headline_features.feature: Text-based editing, Studio Sound, Eye Contact, Green Screen, AI voices and clones, Clips, Avatars, Layouts
headline_features.detail: The homepage feature set: edit the transcript to edit the video, one-click voice enhancement, gaze correction, background removal, voice cloning or stock voices, long-form to short clips, AI avatars, and scene layouts and templates.

Smooths jump cuts with AI. Regenerating a smoothed cut can now target video, audio or both (Aug 2026). 'Smooth all' does every cut at once and is billed per second, 0.5 credit for audio and 1 for video (Sep 2026).

headline_features.feature: Translation and dubbing with lip sync; AI speech
headline_features.detail: Translation offers 'match timing' or direct modes, with an updated lip-sync model (Feb–Mar 2026). Convert to AI Speech replaces a recording's audio with an AI voice. AI Speech moved to ElevenLabs v4, and the voice picker draws on the ElevenLabs voice library. Background music and sound effects can be generated from a description (Sep 2026).

Captions were redesigned with 18 presets, search and filters, and a rebuilt properties panel. There are 15 text animations, usable on any text layer, and gradient fills. Filler-word removal works in Spanish, German, French, Portuguese and Italian.

The API went to open beta with MCP connections in Apr 2026. The Descript MCP is listed in the Claude and ChatGPT directories (Jun 2026). A Zapier app at parity with the API arrived in Sep 2026. Search API and MCP results link straight to projects (Oct 2026).

Generate media through other vendors' models: Seedance 2.0 (Apr), Kling avatars (Apr), Nano Banana 2 and GPT Image 2 images, MiniMax H3 Max Turbo as the default video model on paid plans (Oct). Also YouTube thumbnail generation (Aug) and drawing over an image to edit it with AI.

tools.name: Riverside (Studio, Editor, Magic Clips, Agents)
tools.positioning: A recording-first studio (remote and in-person podcasts, webinars, live) that now edits, clips, publishes, hosts podcasts and runs a team of AI agents. Pricing: free plan (Magic Clips), Pro $29 ($24 annual), Grow $39 ($34; adds MCP and social scheduling), Business custom, with AI credits for generative features. This is from the pricing page, which carried a staging warning.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Locally recorded, separate high-quality tracks per guest, followed by an editor, Magic Clips and publishing in one place. Podcasters can go from recording to clips without leaving it.

headline_features.detail: Four agents. The Producer preps questions, script and studio. The Editor plans the episode edit: it tightens pacing, cuts filler and pauses, switches layouts, adds captions and branding, cleans audio, and suggests B-roll and motion graphics. The Clipper finds moments, including in old recordings. The Marketer writes captions and show notes and schedules posts. They start work without being asked, and 'nothing goes out without your sign-off'. On every plan; web and iOS.

headline_features.feature: Magic Clips from edits; Smooth cuts
headline_features.detail: Magic Clips can now come from your edited version, so clips match the cut you worked on (Oct 28). Smooth cuts uses AI to remove choppy jump cuts so the video plays as one take (Oct 11).

headline_features.feature: Prompted motion graphics, AI B-roll and AI Twin
headline_features.detail: Describe a motion graphic (a logo animation, a lower third) and generate it (Oct 15). Motion graphics for CTAs, graphs and quotes (Jul 27). Image and video generation for B-roll, guest cards and transitions using several models (Sep 17). AI Twin makes an AI version of you from a past recording to speak a script (Sep 7).
Connect Claude or ChatGPT to your account to request clips, edits and posts. On the Grow plan and above.

Video Enhancement (clarity and lighting, Sep 15), Auto-crop that frames speaker tiles (Aug 26), zoom and pan effects (Sep 23), background replacement (Jul 12), more VideoDub languages for correcting spoken mistakes (Jul 14), a teleprompter that follows your voice (Oct 12), a transcript dictionary (Sep 21), and hiding words from captions (Jun 17).

headline_features.feature: In-person multi-camera recording, Mac app editing, social publishing
headline_features.detail: Records a room with several cameras and mics, plus remote guests on synced tracks (Jul 13). The full Editor runs in the native Mac app (Sep 7). Cross-posting with per-post analytics (Aug 18) and video podcasts published to Apple Podcasts (Jul 9).

tools.name: OpusClip
tools.positioning: The leading long-to-short repurposing service: find clips, reframe them, caption them, score them and post them. It is extending into chat editing (AI Producer) and generation (Agent Opus). It claims 16M+ users in its media kit and 20M+ on its homepage. Pricing: Free, Starter $15/mo, Pro $29/mo (multimodal clipping, all aspect ratios, object tracking, AI video B-roll, API, MCP, scheduler), Business custom.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Paste a long video and get dozens of captioned, reframed, scored shorts in minutes, then schedule them, without opening an editor. Reviewers note many of the clips still get thrown away.

headline_features.detail: Finds clips in any genre (vlogs, gaming, sports, interviews) from visuals, sound and emotion as well as speech, and can be steered with a prompt. On Free and Starter, clipping works from spoken words only.
Reframes to 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9 and keeps moving subjects centred by tracking them; you can also choose what to track (tracking needs Pro).

headline_features.feature: Virality score, AI B-roll, Co-Pilot, auto-post and scheduler, export to XML
headline_features.detail: The core feature list in OpusClip's media kit. Brand templates hold fonts, colours, logo and intro/outro.
Edits raw talking-head footage through chat, adding captions, B-roll, motion graphics and sound effects. It also ships as a Codex and Claude Code plugin.

Hosted, with OAuth sign-in. 15 read tools, 14 write tools (edit_clip handles captions, keyword highlighting, filler and pause removal, trims, reordering and dubbing; also posting and scheduling) and 8 media tools (thumbnails, speech, music, video). On Pro, Max and Business plans.

tools.name: Submagic
tools.positioning: Short-form polish for social teams and agencies: animated captions, auto-zoom, B-roll, sound effects, clips, auto edit and publishing. It claims 4M+ businesses. Pricing: Starter $19 ($12 annual), Pro $39 ($23) and Business $69 ($41), metered by video credits, plus API minute packs.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: One click gives the 'viral shorts' look (word captions with emoji, zooms, B-roll, sound effects) and posts it everywhere. It is cheap per video.

headline_features.detail: Applies captions, cuts, pacing and effects to an upload in one click, from a chosen style template.

headline_features.feature: Caption control: custom animations and multi-row editing
headline_features.detail: Custom caption, word and emoji animation styles (Jan 27). Select several caption lines and resize, move, hide or delete them in bulk (Apr 16). Captions in 123 languages.
10M+ new short-form B-roll clips, a Popular Content category and new layouts. Storyblocks B-roll on Pro.
AI Eye Contact (Pro and above), an AI video translator, and Magic Clips, which turns one video into several shorts.

headline_features.feature: MCP server, Find Ideas, Publish + Analytics
headline_features.detail: An MCP server for Claude on your API key (May 6). Find Ideas searches trends and outlier videos and writes scripts in your voice (May 27). Publishing to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, X and Facebook with per-platform AI captions, scheduling and an analytics dashboard (Jun 8).

tools.name: Captions (company now Mirage)
tools.positioning: A mobile-first AI editor for talking-head creators. The company rebranded to Mirage in Sep 2025 as an AI lab building multimodal models, and Mirage Studio (AI actors for ads) has been merged into Captions. It raised $75M on 2026-03-24 and reports 3.2M downloads in the past year, $28.4M in-app revenue and 200M+ videos made. Pricing: freemium app subscription; Mirage's business plan was $399/mo in 2025.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Phone-native: record, then one tap for AI Edit, eye contact, captions and translation. AI twins and avatars make videos without filming.

headline_features.feature: AI Edit and editing by text prompt
headline_features.detail: Pick a style and it edits the whole video, cutting scenes and laying B-roll over them. Further changes are typed as prompts.

headline_features.feature: Eye contact correction, denoise, trim pauses and fillers
headline_features.detail: Fixes stray glances, removes background noise and cuts pauses and filler words.
Make an AI twin of yourself or pick a digital avatar, and change outfit or background by prompt. Mirage Studio is merged in.

headline_features.feature: Translation (100+ languages), generated music and sound effects
headline_features.detail: Translate and subtitle in 100+ languages. Generates royalty-free music and sound effects.

A model trained for pacing, framing and attention in short video, and an audio model that keeps the speaker's accent. Plans to build 'assembly intelligence' models and to merge the mobile and web products.

tools.name: VEED (web editor plus OpenEdit)
tools.positioning: A browser editor for creators and marketing teams that is reaching out to agents: MCP, a ChatGPT app, Make.com, a subtitle API, and OpenEdit, an open-source agent-driven pipeline that runs locally on Apple-silicon Macs with macOS 26. Pricing: freemium, then per-seat subscriptions with monthly AI credits; subtitles unlimited on paid plans within fair use.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Easy in-browser editing with subtitles, translation, lip sync and stock. For developer-creators, OpenEdit is free and agent-native.

headline_features.detail: No GUI and no timeline: a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) composes the edit in HTML and CSS, and VEED Engine renders it locally (VEED says up to 2.2x faster than Chrome-based renderers). It can caption, reframe, add motion graphics, turn slides or sites into video and generate media for credits. Apple Silicon on macOS 26 only. Pipeline Apache-2.0; renderer binaries closed (PolyForm Shield).

headline_features.feature: VEED MCP server, ChatGPT app, Make.com
headline_features.detail: Connects AI assistants and agents so they can create and edit video (Apr 30). Takes a prompt to a finished video inside ChatGPT (May 5). Make.com scenarios (May 7).
Re-dubs a video with your own audio and more natural mouth movement, in Full HD, for videos up to an hour.
Animated caption presets: Handwritten, Whisper, Fusion (Feb 23). Programmatic subtitles in 100+ languages (May 18).

headline_features.feature: GenAI Studio: Kling 3.0 and Multi-Shot; Epidemic Sound
headline_features.detail: Generation from text or images with Kling 3.0 (Feb 6). One prompt to a sequence of camera angles (Apr 23). Epidemic Sound music and sound effects inside the editor (May 6).

tools.name: Kapwing
tools.positioning: A browser editor for teams that has re-centred on Kai, an AI agent that plans and edits and models other vendors' generators, plus an MCP server. Pricing: freemium (4-minute free exports, 50 AI credits), then a subscription with AI credits; MCP at no extra cost.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: A collaborative web editor with strong subtitles, translation and dubbing, an agent that shows the cost before it acts, and no install.

headline_features.detail: A task checklist with progress shown on the canvas. You approve the estimated credit cost first and can interrupt with a refund. Kai checks its own output and corrects errors, states its limits, and reads uploads (waveform peaks, transcripts) before planning. Faceswaps of real people are refused.

headline_features.feature: Multimodal moment finding and speaker smart crop
headline_features.detail: Kai assembles clips from visual and audio cues (example: 'Find the dunks from the third quarter') and keeps a speaker in frame. The agent's plan shows cost, prompts and models before you confirm, and plans under 40 credits are accepted automatically.
12 new presets (Editorial, Scribble, Zing). Line length follows the aspect ratio: short and bold for vertical, longer for landscape. New animations: Growing, Vibrate, Typing and Word Fly.

1.0 for all users on Oct 12 and 1.1 on Oct 27. Tools upload, create projects, export, caption, transcribe, translate, dub, generate images and video, and edit through the transcript or by placing layers in natural language. Each MCP project opens as an editable Kai chat.
AI blur of moving objects from a text prompt, such as 'blur faces' or 'blur license plates'.

tools.name: Canva (video editor, Magic Video, Canva AI 2.0)
tools.positioning: Design-first, template-and-brand-kit video for marketers and social teams, inside the tool they already use for graphics. Pricing: free, then Canva Pro or Teams subscriptions, with monthly AI usage limits on premium AI.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Brand kits, huge template libraries and team workflows. Video is 'good enough' for social and sits next to every other asset. Weak on precise editing; one review notes no chroma key.

headline_features.detail: Upload footage and describe the result; it assembles a social-ready edit of up to 60 s with cuts, synced audio and transitions. On all plans, including free, with an hourly limit; cropping may miss the subject.
headline_features.as_of: 2026-11-01 (help page returned 403 to the fetcher; details are from the search snippet)

headline_features.detail: Text-to-video clips with synced sound on Google's Veo 3, for paid plans.

Conversational design, iterative agentic editing, layered object intelligence and 'living memory'. Third-party coverage of Canva Create also names Magic Video 2.0, AI video effects and caption styles.

tools.name: Edits (Meta / Instagram)
tools.positioning: A free platform-owned mobile editor (launched Apr 2025) that competes with CapCut. Desktop version announced. Pricing: free, no watermark; more AI assistant usage through a Meta One subscription.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Free, no watermark, made for Reels, and tied to Instagram data: an assistant that reads your own Reels performance, weekly ideas from past Reels, and links to IG accounts and Reels.

headline_features.detail: Reads your follows, views, retention, likes, shares, comments and Instagram trends; suggests audio and concepts that performed. Meta positions it as an analyst: 'the creative calls are still yours'. Free with a usage cap; Meta One for more.
Previewed with project sync between phone and desktop; 'coming soon', operating systems not stated.
Clickable IG account and Reel links in exports, 25 video effects, 10 weekly content ideas from past Reels, and multiple takes on the storyboard.

headline_features.feature: Free AI translation with lip sync on Instagram
headline_features.detail: Dubs the creator's voice and matches the lips, free for public accounts, in 14 languages after the July 2026 expansion (Japanese, Korean, French, German, Italian). Platform-side, not inside Edits.

tools.name: YouTube Create / Shorts editor / YouTube Studio
tools.positioning: Free editing and AI built into the platform. Pricing: free.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Free, publishes straight to YouTube, and auto-dubbing and A/B tests run where the audience is.

headline_features.detail: Chat-driven editing for Shorts and the Create app: picks the best takes, adds music and transitions, inserts text, removes pauses, and moves to the manual timeline when you want. YouTube's words: 'edits with you, not for you'.
Opened to all creators in 27 languages (Feb 2026), with Expressive Speech in 8 languages. Lip sync is still a pilot with select channels. Real-time dubbing for live streams is in testing.

headline_features.feature: Studio: video A/B tests, three thumbnails, Ask Studio
headline_features.detail: Test different edits; up to three thumbnails per video; an AI that drafts brand pitches.

headline_features.feature: Edit with AI (first-draft Shorts from the camera roll)
headline_features.detail: Turns camera-roll footage into a first-draft Short in the YouTube app and in Create (Android).

tools.name: Adobe Premiere (iPhone and Android app; Premiere Pro desktop)
tools.positioning: Adobe's free creator-grade mobile editor, as a funnel to Premiere Pro, with Firefly generative AI on credits. Pricing: the app and exports are free; generative features use Firefly credits.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Free unlimited 4K exports with no watermark, an Adobe-quality timeline, and a path to desktop Premiere Pro.

headline_features.detail: Unlimited free auto captions, one-tap background removal, Enhance Audio, templates for YouTube Shorts with direct publishing, and unlimited 4K exports without a watermark. On iOS and Android.
Record timing with your voice and AI makes a matching sound effect. Firefly makes stickers, images, extended backgrounds and clips. iOS only; uses credits.
Extends a clip with generated frames (launched Jan 2026). In 26.5 it takes more source media (360p to 4K, any aspect, interlaced) and adds a Generative Media tool.

tools.name: Final Cut Pro 12 / Apple Creator Studio
tools.positioning: Apple's pro editor, now in a creator subscription bundle with on-device intelligence on Apple silicon. Pricing: Creator Studio is $12.99/mo or $129/yr (Final Cut Pro, Logic, Pixelmator Pro, Motion, Compressor, MainStage); the Mac app can still be bought once.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Fast native editing on the Mac, Apple-silicon performance, and now semantic search and captions. The iPad versions come only with the subscription.

headline_features.feature: Transcript Search, Visual Search, Beat Detection (12.0)
headline_features.detail: Find spoken phrases (exact or natural-language), find objects and actions by description (both need Apple silicon), and map a song's bars and beats for cutting to music.

headline_features.feature: Generate Captions, Auto Mask, Match Color, Edit Detection, Pixelmator Pro hand-off (12.3)
headline_features.detail: Captions you can restyle for social platforms, US English only. Isolate recognised objects for grading. Match colour across cameras. Split rendered video at its shot changes. Send a frame to Pixelmator Pro for thumbnails.
Launched 2026-01-28 with a 1-month trial, Family Sharing and a $2.99 student tier.

tools.name: DaVinci Resolve 21 / 21.1
tools.positioning: A free pro editor, Studio for $295 once, adding AI tools and, in 21.1, a native MCP server for AI assistants. Pricing: free; Studio a one-time $295.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Free, with pro grading, Fairlight audio and, in Studio, AI tools that need no subscription.

headline_features.detail: File ▸ Setup AI Assistants connects Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok. Uses: project analysis, media organisation, project settings and batch renders. Blackmagic warns that scripts an AI assistant writes have the assistant's own system access. A Studio feature.

headline_features.feature: IntelliSearch, IntelliScript, AI Speech Generator, CineFocus, face tools
headline_features.detail: Search footage for people, objects, faces and dialogue. Build a timeline from a script (Final Draft or text). Generate speech from text with a voice sampled from your own clip. AI focus and depth-of-field changes. Face age, reshaping and blemish tools. AI Motion Deblur and UltraSharpen.

tools.name: Screen Studio 4 (with ScreenKite and Prequel as challengers)
tools.positioning: The leading polished-screencast editor on the Mac (auto zooms, cursor, camera), which in 4.0 became a talking-head and creator editor too. Pricing: $29/mo or $9/mo billed yearly; the one-time licence was withdrawn in Oct 2025. ScreenKite: free tier with a watermark, $79.99 once ($99.99 after Oct 31, 2026). Prequel: $9/mo or $39 once.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Screencasts that look professional with no editing: automatic zooms and cursor smoothing. In 4.0, transcript cuts, captions and on-device camera tools came too.

headline_features.feature: Edit by transcript, filler and pause removal, captions
headline_features.detail: Delete words to cut the video, find ums, uhs and long pauses, and style captions line by line or word by word with word animations. Transcription is in the cloud (needs macOS 26 and an account).

Camera cutout (background removal on your Mac, beta), split screen with animated layout switches, face tracking, colour grading with 12 looks and your own LUTs, a glass loupe and sharper zooms through an on-device upscaler, and on-device noise reduction and 'Podcast' voice (beta).

headline_features.feature: Privacy masking and face blur, ProRes export (4.1)
headline_features.detail: Automatically hides emails, phone numbers, card numbers and keys, and blurs faces. ProRes export.
Use Screen Studio from Claude or Cursor; AI voiceover; multi-clip recordings.

headline_features.feature: ScreenKite: native Swift recorder and editor with 83 local agent tools
headline_features.detail: A multi-track timeline, transcript cutting, auto zoom and word-highlight captions. Coding agents (Claude Code, Codex and others) edit projects through 83 local tools, billed to the user's own agent plan with no ScreenKite AI fee. Risky edits return a plan first and apply on a second call. This is the founder's own blog.

tools.name: AI rough-cut assistants that hand off to a pro editor (Gling, Eddie AI, Selects by Cutback)
tools.positioning: A layer before the edit: transcribe, cut silences and bad takes, sync multicam, then export a project to Premiere, Final Cut Pro or Resolve. Pricing: Gling free tier then about $10–20/mo; Eddie credit packs; Selects free hand-off with paid analysis and multicam (all from third-party or vendor pages).
tools.why_creators_pick_it: YouTubers and podcast editors keep their own editor but skip the tedious assembly.

headline_features.detail: Removes bad takes, silences and fillers. Text-based trimming, captions, auto zoom, YouTube titles and chapters, and export to Final Cut Pro, Resolve and Premiere (plus MP4, MP3, SRT).
Syncs up to 6 cameras and cuts to whoever is speaking. Exports to Premiere, Resolve and Final Cut Pro with the angles still switchable. A full podcast cut cannot be re-prompted.

headline_features.feature: Selects by Cutback: pre-edit with MCP
headline_features.detail: Transcription that respects breaths, scene and speaker-angle detection, multicam sync, filler and bad-take removal, B-roll insertion and parallel variant renders. Connects to Claude over MCP and exports native FCPXML and Resolve and Premiere projects.

tools.name: Agent-written video frameworks (HeyGen HyperFrames, Remotion)
tools.positioning: Video as code for coding agents: the agent writes HTML or React and a deterministic renderer makes the MP4. Used for motion graphics, product videos and captions rather than cutting camera footage. Pricing: HyperFrames Apache-2.0 and free; Remotion source-available, with company licences above small-team thresholds.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Developer-creators and agents can make on-brand motion graphics and explainers from a prompt, reproducibly.

headline_features.detail: 'Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.' Seeks each frame in headless Chrome and encodes with FFmpeg, with animation from GSAP, CSS, Lottie or Three.js. Ships 7 agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI. About 76.6k GitHub stars; released 2026-04-17 per the third-party comparisons.
React-for-video projects authored by Claude Code through Remotion's agent skills.

trends.trend: Agentic and conversational editing is the new front door. The pattern that won: plan, show the cost, get approval, apply, check itself, then fall back to the timeline.
trends.evidence: Descript's Underlord runs an automatic review pass after each editing turn (May 2026) and states its plans in plain language (Oct 2026). Kapwing's Kai shows the cost and models of an editable plan, asks for approval, refunds on interrupt and checks its own output (Mar and Aug 2026). Riverside's four Agents start work unprompted but 'nothing goes out without your sign-off' (2026-10-26). YouTube's conversational editor 'edits with you, not for you' and opens onto the manual timeline (announced 2026-09-23, early 2027). CapCut EditPilot is shipped on desktop, and an agentic goal-to-first-draft mode is piloting (2026-10-27). OpusClip's AI Producer is in open beta. Canva AI 2.0 is a research preview (Apr 2026). ScreenKite applies a risky edit only on a second call.

trends.trend: MCP went from novelty to expected in 2026. Almost every AI-forward editor now exposes itself to Claude and ChatGPT, so having an MCP surface no longer sets a tool apart; depth, accuracy and running locally will.
trends.evidence: Descript: API and MCP (Apr 2026), listed in the Claude and ChatGPT directories (Jun 2026). VEED MCP (2026-04-30) and a ChatGPT app (2026-05-05). Submagic MCP (2026-05-06). OpusClip: hosted MCP with 37 tools. Riverside MCP (2026-08-31). Kapwing MCP 1.0 (2026-10-12) and 1.1 (2026-10-27). DaVinci Resolve 21.1 has a built-in MCP server in Studio (2026-09-08). Screen Studio's MCP server is in progress. ScreenKite has 83 local agent tools. CapCut-in-ChatGPT is due 'in the coming months'.

trends.trend: Editors resell other vendors' generative models (B-roll, images, music, sound effects, avatars), billed in credits.
trends.evidence: Descript: Seedance 2.0, Kling avatars, MiniMax H3 as default, GPT Image 2, Nano Banana 2, ElevenLabs, and generated music and sound effects. Kapwing: Seedance 2.5, MiniMax H3 as Kai's default, Grok. Riverside: AI image and video generation for B-roll and transitions (Sep 2026). VEED: Kling 3.0 and Multi-Shot. Canva: Veo 3. CapCut: its own Seedance, Seedream and Seed Audio. OpusClip: AI video B-roll on Pro.

trends.trend: The repurposing pipeline is now one product: long-form, find clips, reframe, caption, B-roll, publish or schedule, analytics.
trends.evidence: OpusClip: ClipAnything, ReframeAnything, virality score, auto-post and scheduler. Riverside: Magic Clips from edits, cross-posting with analytics, and a Clipper and a Marketer agent. Submagic: Magic Clips plus Publish + Analytics on 6 platforms (2026-06-08) and trend research through Find Ideas. Descript: Create Clips, YouTube and LinkedIn publishing.

trends.trend: AI fixes that make the speaker look and sound better are now expected in creator AI tools: eye contact, voice enhancement, filler and pause removal, smoothed jump cuts.
trends.evidence: Eye contact: Descript, Captions, Submagic Pro, Riverside Pro. Smoothed jump cuts: Descript 'Smooth all' (Sep 2026) and Riverside Smooth cuts (2026-10-11). Filler removal in 5 extra languages (Descript, Aug 2026). CapCut EditPilot does filler removal, noise reduction and loudness normalisation. Screen Studio 4 does filler and pause removal.

trends.trend: Voice and likeness work (clones, AI twins, lip-synced dubbing) is spreading fast. Translation and dubbing are being given away by the platforms themselves.
trends.evidence: Riverside AI Twin (Sep 2026). Captions/Mirage AI twin and avatars. Descript ElevenLabs voice clones, Convert to AI Speech and lip-synced translation. VEED Lipsync 2.0 (Jul 2026). Resolve 21's AI Speech Generator with a voice sampled from your own clip. Meanwhile YouTube auto-dubbing opened to all creators in 27 languages (Feb 2026), and Instagram's lip-synced AI translation is free in 14 languages (Jul 2026).

trends.trend: Captions have become a design system: many presets, word and emoji animations, editing many lines at once, line length that follows the aspect ratio.
trends.evidence: Descript: 18 presets and 15 text animations (Sep 2026). Kapwing: 12 presets, aspect-aware line length and 4 animations (Aug 2026). VEED Dynamic Subtitles (Feb 2026). Submagic: custom caption animations (Jan 2026) and multi-row editing (Apr 2026). Screen Studio 4: word-by-word captions with animations.

trends.trend: Platforms give away capable editors and tie them to performance data. That squeezes paid mid-tier editors as CapCut's price rises.
trends.evidence: Edits is free with no watermark, and its assistant reads your own Reels analytics (2026-09-30); a desktop version is announced. YouTube Create and Shorts get a conversational editor (2027) and video A/B tests. Premiere mobile is free with unlimited 4K exports. CapCut Pro is now $179.99/yr, up from about $78 in Feb 2026, and Auto Reframe moved behind Pro (Apr 2026).

trends.trend: Search by meaning and on-device machine learning are arriving in Mac editors, and 'runs on your Mac' is used as a selling point.
trends.evidence: Final Cut Pro 12: Transcript Search and Visual Search on Apple silicon (Jan 2026), then Auto Mask, Match Color and Edit Detection (Jun 2026). Resolve IntelliSearch. CapCut Smart Search. Screen Studio 4 markets its on-device cutout, upscaler and noise reduction. VEED OpenEdit renders locally on Apple-silicon macOS 26.

trends.trend: Screencast tools and creator editors are converging on one feature set: transcript cuts, camera cutout, split screen, captions, privacy masking, agents.
trends.evidence: Screen Studio 4.0 (2026-10-02) added transcript editing, camera cutout, split screen, face tracking and LUT grading; 4.1 added data masking and face blur, with an MCP server in progress. ScreenKite (Swift, 83 agent tools, one-time price) and Prequel (transcript editing from Sep 2026, lifetime licence) compete on agents and on price.

trends.trend: Credit-metered subscriptions are everywhere, alongside a visible market for one-time, free and open-source alternatives.
trends.evidence: Separate meters for credits and media hours (Descript), AI credits (Riverside, Kapwing, CapCut, VEED) and per-video credits (Submagic). Against that: Screen Studio dropped its one-time licence, while ScreenKite ($79.99 once), Prequel ($39 lifetime), Resolve Studio ($295 once) and VEED OpenEdit (free, Apache-2.0 pipeline) sell on not having a subscription. OpenCut, the open-source CapCut alternative, has about 96K GitHub stars while mid-rewrite.

trends.trend: Multicam podcast and interview editing with automatic cuts to the active speaker is a hot workflow.
trends.evidence: Riverside in-person multi-camera recording (Jul 2026) with an Editor agent that switches layouts. Eddie AI syncs up to 6 cameras and cuts to the active speaker. Selects syncs multicam and detects speakers. Resolve 21.1 improved multi-camera workflows. (Frame Job's spec scope excludes multicam; the owner has said that limit can be lifted.)

trends.trend: Video as code for agents: motion graphics and explainers written as HTML or React by coding agents and rendered deterministically.
trends.evidence: HeyGen HyperFrames (Apache-2.0, about 76.6k stars, agent skills). Remotion's Claude Code plugin. VEED OpenEdit (an agent writes HTML and CSS, rendered locally). Riverside's prompted motion graphics (Oct 2026). Frame Job's JavaScript graphic modules are in the same family.

table_stakes: Auto captions in a word-by-word social style with many presets and animations, keyword and emoji highlighting, editable text, several languages and SRT export. Every surveyed creator tool ships this. Frame Job today: has on-device or AssemblyAI captions, five word styles and SRT/VTT, so it has the base but few presets and animations compared with Descript's 18 presets and 15 animations or Kapwing's 12 presets.

Editing by transcript: delete words in the transcript to cut the video (Descript, Riverside, Screen Studio 4, ScreenKite, Gling, Kapwing, Captions). Frame Job today: Remove Filler Words and get_transcript exist, but docs/guide describes no editor where you work on the transcript itself.

One-click cleanup of speech: filler-word and silence removal plus smoothing of the jump cuts that leaves (Descript 'Smooth all', Riverside Smooth cuts). Frame Job has the first two; smoothing jump cuts is missing.
One-click voice enhancement, noise removal and loudness normalisation (Studio Sound, Enhance Audio, CapCut EditPilot). Frame Job is strong here: Enhance Voice, voice isolation, normalisation to LUFS.

Aspect-ratio conversion with subject-tracking auto reframe to 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9 (OpusClip ReframeAnything, CapCut Auto Reframe, Kapwing smart crop, Riverside Auto-crop, Screen Studio face tracking). Frame Job has vertical and square presets and a blurred background, but no tracking reframe.

Background removal and person cutout without a green screen (CapCut Auto Cutout, Descript Green Screen, Premiere mobile, Screen Studio camera cutout, Riverside background replacement), plus chroma key.
Long-form to short clips: finding moments in talking heads at least, and increasingly from what is seen and heard (OpusClip, Riverside Magic Clips, Descript Clips, Submagic Magic Clips, Kapwing).

Brand kit and templates: fonts, colours, logo, intros and outros, caption presets (OpusClip brand templates, Submagic branded intros and outros, Riverside Personalize hub, Canva brand kits, CapCut templates).

Libraries of royalty-free music, sound effects and stock B-roll, increasingly with generated B-roll (Submagic B-Rolls 2.0, VEED Epidemic Sound, Riverside sound effects, Descript generated music and sound effects).
Automatic zooms and punch-ins on talking heads and screencasts (Submagic auto-zoom, Gling auto zoom, Screen Studio, Riverside zoom and pan).
Eye-contact correction, standard in the creator AI tier (Descript, Captions, Submagic Pro, Riverside Pro).
Translated subtitles at minimum. Dubbing with lip sync is increasingly expected but is being commoditised by YouTube and Instagram doing it free on the platform.
Social export presets and, increasingly, direct publishing and scheduling to TikTok, Reels, Shorts, YouTube and LinkedIn (Submagic, Riverside, OpusClip, Descript, Premiere mobile to YouTube).
A natural-language assistant that edits with a visible plan, cost approval and undo, and hands off to a precise timeline (Underlord, Kai, EditPilot, Riverside Agents). Frame Job has the Assistant.
An MCP server or API for outside agents, now standard among AI-forward tools (Descript, VEED, Kapwing, OpusClip, Submagic, Riverside, Resolve 21.1). Frame Job already has one.
A free way in with watermark-free export, or at least a real trial, because Edits, Premiere mobile and YouTube Create set the bar at free.
differentiators: Trustworthy agent editing rather than having an agent at all. Everyone now has a chat box and an MCP server; what still separates tools is whether the agent's edits are precise, can be undone, can be inspected and are checked by the agent itself. Reviewers say OpusClip users discard many clips, and Eddie cannot re-prompt a full cut. The leaders add self-review passes (Descript, Kapwing), an editable plan with its cost (Kapwing, ScreenKite) and approval gates (Riverside). An editor whose every agent edit is a pure, undoable, frame-accurate op that the agent can render back and check (Frame Job's model: ops that answer applied, identity or refused; render_frame) has a real edge, if it is packaged as a workflow creators can see.

Understanding the content beyond the transcript. Finding moments from what is seen and heard (ClipAnything; Kapwing's 'find the dunks'; Final Cut Pro Visual Search and Resolve IntelliSearch on Apple silicon) separates tools from transcript-only clippers. On a Mac this can run on the device (Vision, Sound Analysis, Speech) at no per-minute cost, which hosted competitors cannot match on price or privacy.

A complete repurposing loop in one place: long-form, to ranked clips, to tracked reframe, to captions and B-roll, to a brand template, to export variants for each platform. OpusClip, Riverside and Submagic win creators on this loop, not on timeline depth. A desktop editor that does the whole loop locally and keeps everything open to fine editing would be unusual.

Speaker fixes as one finishing pass: eye contact, Studio-Sound-quality voice, smoothed jump cuts, lighting and clarity enhancement (Riverside Video Enhancement, Descript Portrait Lighting). Creators pick Descript, Captions and Riverside for 'make me look and sound good with one button'.

Price and ownership model. CapCut Pro is now $179.99/yr, Screen Studio is subscription-only since Oct 2025, and every AI tool meters credits. Meanwhile ScreenKite ($79.99 once, AI billed to the user's own agent plan), Prequel (lifetime), Resolve Studio (one-time) and VEED OpenEdit (free, agent-native, Apple-silicon macOS 26) sell on 'no subscription'. Open source, bring-your-own-key, on-device by default and no credits is a real differentiator, already partly held by Frame Job, if it is made visible to creators.

Finishing quality the web creator tools lack: true colour management and HDR deliverables, 10-bit and ProRes or AV1 exports, LUT grading, accurate loudness and stems. Creator tools are weak here (Canva, Kapwing, VEED are browser-based; one Canva review notes no chroma key), and pro editors (Final Cut Pro, Resolve) have the finish but not the creator-AI workflow. Combining the two is the gap Final Cut Pro 12 and Resolve 21.1 are moving into from the pro side.

Screencast-specific polish (auto zoom, cursor, camera cutout, split screen with animated layout changes, privacy masking of emails and keys, face blur). Screen Studio 4 shows this is a buying reason in its own right, and it is Frame Job's home segment.

Multicam podcast and interview automation (sync, cut to the active speaker, switchable angles) wins the podcast and video-podcast segment (Riverside, Eddie, Selects). It is currently outside Frame Job's spec scope, which the owner says may be lifted.

Tools to build an audience: performance-aware suggestions (Edits assistant, Submagic Find Ideas, YouTube A/B testing). Platform-native tools have the data advantage. A desktop editor can at most generate titles, chapters and thumbnails and export A/B variants.

Ecosystem scale: CapCut's 400,000+ templates a day and Skills Marketplace, and Canva's template and brand network. This is a network effect a single-developer project cannot copy. The plausible counter is agent-written, shareable graphic modules (the HyperFrames and Remotion pattern, and Frame Job's .fjgraphic) that an agent can make on demand.

toolu_012wLu6JpwXG4ERPnRdYzT94.segment: Creator-first video editors and AI repurposing tools as of 1 November 2026. This covers the mass-market editors (CapCut, Canva, Edits, YouTube Create, Premiere mobile), the AI editors built around a transcript or an agent (Descript, Riverside, Kapwing, VEED, Captions/Mirage), the short-form clip makers (OpusClip, Submagic), the screencast editors (Screen Studio 4, ScreenKite), the AI rough-cut assistants that hand off to a pro editor (Gling, Eddie AI, Selects), the pro editors as they chase creators (Final Cut Pro 12 / Apple Creator Studio, DaVinci Resolve 21.1), and the agent-written video frameworks (VEED OpenEdit, HeyGen HyperFrames). Pricing is given in one phrase in each tool's positioning field. Status is "shipped", "beta" or "announced", taken from the vendor's own wording where it gives one. Most of the 2026 detail comes from vendor changelogs fetched on 2026-11-01: Descript's Canny changelog, Riverside's product-updates page, VEED's changelog, Kapwing's monthly release notes, Submagic's Canny changelog, CapCut's newsroom, and Apple's Final Cut Pro release notes. A claim that rests only on third-party coverage is marked as such.

tools.name: CapCut (desktop, web, mobile; Standard / Pro / Ultra)
tools.positioning: The default mass-market editor (660M+ users in 170+ markets), now also ByteDance's AI generation front end (Seedance video, Seedream images, Seed Audio) with an agent layer arriving. In the US it runs under the TikTok USDS joint venture, closed 2026-01-22. Pricing: free core, then Pro at $19.99/mo or $179.99/yr (the annual price was about $78 before Feb 2026) with about 1,200 AI credits, Standard at $9.99 (mobile, regional) and Ultra at about $79/mo (third-party price trackers, Oct 2026).
tools.why_creators_pick_it: It is free or cheap on phone, desktop and web, with a huge template, effects and sound library tied to TikTok trends (400,000+ new templates a day), auto captions, and fast results. Most short-form creators already know it.

headline_features.detail: An assistant inside the multi-track editor. You describe an edit and it removes filler words, rough-trims talking heads, writes captions (bilingual where supported), emphasises key lines, reduces noise, enhances the voice and normalises loudness. English first. CapCut says it is not a one-click video maker and that you review its changes on the timeline. The Oct 2026 update adds prompt edits such as recolouring one object in a shot. A third party (hokai.io) says it is bundled into Pro.

headline_features.feature: Agentic creation, ChatGPT plugin, Skills Marketplace
headline_features.detail: An agent that turns a creative goal into a first draft on desktop, web and mobile, piloting 'in the coming months'. CapCut inside ChatGPT, also 'in the coming months'. A web marketplace for sharing reusable creative workflows ('Skills'). An AI-provenance checker is in pilot.

Smart Search (find clips by objects, speech, people and places), Auto Captions, Remove Filler Words, Scene Detection, Auto Cutout (background removal), chroma key, keyframes and graphs, colour grading (LUTs, wheels, skin-tone protection), selfie retouching with face tracking, Script to Video and text-to-speech.
Auto Reframe (subject-aware aspect-ratio change) moved from a free preview to Pro on desktop, web and mobile. Basic crop and zoom stay free.

headline_features.feature: Generative studios: Video Studio, Director Mode, Design Studio
headline_features.detail: Seedance interactive editing changes one timestamp, character or element without regenerating the scene. Director Mode takes an AI short drama from script to characters to shots to assembled edit; it is on CapCut Web globally, with the US rollout 'coming soon'. Design Studio has an infinite canvas and Skills. CapCut reports 6B+ AI outputs in 2026 and 7M+ creators using its AI features daily.
headline_features.status: shipped (Director Mode: not yet in the US)

tools.name: Descript
tools.positioning: Editing video by editing its transcript, now led by Underlord, an agentic co-editor that offers a choice of models, plus recording (Rooms), publishing and an API with an MCP server. Aimed at podcasters, YouTubers, educators and marketing teams. Pricing: free plan, then Hobbyist $24 ($16 annual), Creator $35 ($24) and Business $65 ($50) per seat, metered by media hours plus AI credits (third-party summary, checked against Descript's pricing on 2026-08-20).
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Cutting a talk by deleting words is the fastest edit there is, and Studio Sound, Eye Contact, filler removal and AI voice fixes come in one place. Underlord does the first pass. It works well for podcasts and talking-head YouTube.

headline_features.detail: Underlord v2 (Jan 2026) used about 20% fewer credits for a full edit. It lets you pick the model (Claude, Gemini, GPT; Claude Opus 5.5 is the Enterprise default). Each editing turn now gets an automatic review pass (May 2026), and since Oct 2026 Underlord states its plans in plain language. It previews audio and video before applying (Mar 2026). It has a Revert button, an @ context picker and per-project chat history.

headline_features.feature: Text-based editing, Studio Sound, Eye Contact, Green Screen, AI voices and clones, Clips, Avatars, Layouts
headline_features.detail: The homepage feature set: edit the transcript to edit the video, one-click voice enhancement, gaze correction, background removal, voice cloning or stock voices, long-form to short clips, AI avatars, and scene layouts and templates.

Smooths jump cuts with AI. Regenerating a smoothed cut can now target video, audio or both (Aug 2026). 'Smooth all' does every cut at once and is billed per second, 0.5 credit for audio and 1 for video (Sep 2026).

headline_features.feature: Translation and dubbing with lip sync; AI speech
headline_features.detail: Translation offers 'match timing' or direct modes, with an updated lip-sync model (Feb–Mar 2026). Convert to AI Speech replaces a recording's audio with an AI voice. AI Speech moved to ElevenLabs v4, and the voice picker draws on the ElevenLabs voice library. Background music and sound effects can be generated from a description (Sep 2026).

Captions were redesigned with 18 presets, search and filters, and a rebuilt properties panel. There are 15 text animations, usable on any text layer, and gradient fills. Filler-word removal works in Spanish, German, French, Portuguese and Italian.

The API went to open beta with MCP connections in Apr 2026. The Descript MCP is listed in the Claude and ChatGPT directories (Jun 2026). A Zapier app at parity with the API arrived in Sep 2026. Search API and MCP results link straight to projects (Oct 2026).

Generate media through other vendors' models: Seedance 2.0 (Apr), Kling avatars (Apr), Nano Banana 2 and GPT Image 2 images, MiniMax H3 Max Turbo as the default video model on paid plans (Oct). Also YouTube thumbnail generation (Aug) and drawing over an image to edit it with AI.

tools.name: Riverside (Studio, Editor, Magic Clips, Agents)
tools.positioning: A recording-first studio (remote and in-person podcasts, webinars, live) that now edits, clips, publishes, hosts podcasts and runs a team of AI agents. Pricing: free plan (Magic Clips), Pro $29 ($24 annual), Grow $39 ($34; adds MCP and social scheduling), Business custom, with AI credits for generative features. This is from the pricing page, which carried a staging warning.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Locally recorded, separate high-quality tracks per guest, followed by an editor, Magic Clips and publishing in one place. Podcasters can go from recording to clips without leaving it.

headline_features.detail: Four agents. The Producer preps questions, script and studio. The Editor plans the episode edit: it tightens pacing, cuts filler and pauses, switches layouts, adds captions and branding, cleans audio, and suggests B-roll and motion graphics. The Clipper finds moments, including in old recordings. The Marketer writes captions and show notes and schedules posts. They start work without being asked, and 'nothing goes out without your sign-off'. On every plan; web and iOS.

headline_features.feature: Magic Clips from edits; Smooth cuts
headline_features.detail: Magic Clips can now come from your edited version, so clips match the cut you worked on (Oct 28). Smooth cuts uses AI to remove choppy jump cuts so the video plays as one take (Oct 11).

headline_features.feature: Prompted motion graphics, AI B-roll and AI Twin
headline_features.detail: Describe a motion graphic (a logo animation, a lower third) and generate it (Oct 15). Motion graphics for CTAs, graphs and quotes (Jul 27). Image and video generation for B-roll, guest cards and transitions using several models (Sep 17). AI Twin makes an AI version of you from a past recording to speak a script (Sep 7).
Connect Claude or ChatGPT to your account to request clips, edits and posts. On the Grow plan and above.

Video Enhancement (clarity and lighting, Sep 15), Auto-crop that frames speaker tiles (Aug 26), zoom and pan effects (Sep 23), background replacement (Jul 12), more VideoDub languages for correcting spoken mistakes (Jul 14), a teleprompter that follows your voice (Oct 12), a transcript dictionary (Sep 21), and hiding words from captions (Jun 17).

headline_features.feature: In-person multi-camera recording, Mac app editing, social publishing
headline_features.detail: Records a room with several cameras and mics, plus remote guests on synced tracks (Jul 13). The full Editor runs in the native Mac app (Sep 7). Cross-posting with per-post analytics (Aug 18) and video podcasts published to Apple Podcasts (Jul 9).

tools.name: OpusClip
tools.positioning: The leading long-to-short repurposing service: find clips, reframe them, caption them, score them and post them. It is extending into chat editing (AI Producer) and generation (Agent Opus). It claims 16M+ users in its media kit and 20M+ on its homepage. Pricing: Free, Starter $15/mo, Pro $29/mo (multimodal clipping, all aspect ratios, object tracking, AI video B-roll, API, MCP, scheduler), Business custom.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Paste a long video and get dozens of captioned, reframed, scored shorts in minutes, then schedule them, without opening an editor. Reviewers note many of the clips still get thrown away.

headline_features.detail: Finds clips in any genre (vlogs, gaming, sports, interviews) from visuals, sound and emotion as well as speech, and can be steered with a prompt. On Free and Starter, clipping works from spoken words only.
Reframes to 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9 and keeps moving subjects centred by tracking them; you can also choose what to track (tracking needs Pro).

headline_features.feature: Virality score, AI B-roll, Co-Pilot, auto-post and scheduler, export to XML
headline_features.detail: The core feature list in OpusClip's media kit. Brand templates hold fonts, colours, logo and intro/outro.
Edits raw talking-head footage through chat, adding captions, B-roll, motion graphics and sound effects. It also ships as a Codex and Claude Code plugin.

Hosted, with OAuth sign-in. 15 read tools, 14 write tools (edit_clip handles captions, keyword highlighting, filler and pause removal, trims, reordering and dubbing; also posting and scheduling) and 8 media tools (thumbnails, speech, music, video). On Pro, Max and Business plans.

tools.name: Submagic
tools.positioning: Short-form polish for social teams and agencies: animated captions, auto-zoom, B-roll, sound effects, clips, auto edit and publishing. It claims 4M+ businesses. Pricing: Starter $19 ($12 annual), Pro $39 ($23) and Business $69 ($41), metered by video credits, plus API minute packs.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: One click gives the 'viral shorts' look (word captions with emoji, zooms, B-roll, sound effects) and posts it everywhere. It is cheap per video.

headline_features.detail: Applies captions, cuts, pacing and effects to an upload in one click, from a chosen style template.

headline_features.feature: Caption control: custom animations and multi-row editing
headline_features.detail: Custom caption, word and emoji animation styles (Jan 27). Select several caption lines and resize, move, hide or delete them in bulk (Apr 16). Captions in 123 languages.
10M+ new short-form B-roll clips, a Popular Content category and new layouts. Storyblocks B-roll on Pro.
AI Eye Contact (Pro and above), an AI video translator, and Magic Clips, which turns one video into several shorts.

headline_features.feature: MCP server, Find Ideas, Publish + Analytics
headline_features.detail: An MCP server for Claude on your API key (May 6). Find Ideas searches trends and outlier videos and writes scripts in your voice (May 27). Publishing to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, X and Facebook with per-platform AI captions, scheduling and an analytics dashboard (Jun 8).

tools.name: Captions (company now Mirage)
tools.positioning: A mobile-first AI editor for talking-head creators. The company rebranded to Mirage in Sep 2025 as an AI lab building multimodal models, and Mirage Studio (AI actors for ads) has been merged into Captions. It raised $75M on 2026-03-24 and reports 3.2M downloads in the past year, $28.4M in-app revenue and 200M+ videos made. Pricing: freemium app subscription; Mirage's business plan was $399/mo in 2025.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Phone-native: record, then one tap for AI Edit, eye contact, captions and translation. AI twins and avatars make videos without filming.

headline_features.feature: AI Edit and editing by text prompt
headline_features.detail: Pick a style and it edits the whole video, cutting scenes and laying B-roll over them. Further changes are typed as prompts.

headline_features.feature: Eye contact correction, denoise, trim pauses and fillers
headline_features.detail: Fixes stray glances, removes background noise and cuts pauses and filler words.
Make an AI twin of yourself or pick a digital avatar, and change outfit or background by prompt. Mirage Studio is merged in.

headline_features.feature: Translation (100+ languages), generated music and sound effects
headline_features.detail: Translate and subtitle in 100+ languages. Generates royalty-free music and sound effects.

A model trained for pacing, framing and attention in short video, and an audio model that keeps the speaker's accent. Plans to build 'assembly intelligence' models and to merge the mobile and web products.

tools.name: VEED (web editor plus OpenEdit)
tools.positioning: A browser editor for creators and marketing teams that is reaching out to agents: MCP, a ChatGPT app, Make.com, a subtitle API, and OpenEdit, an open-source agent-driven pipeline that runs locally on Apple-silicon Macs with macOS 26. Pricing: freemium, then per-seat subscriptions with monthly AI credits; subtitles unlimited on paid plans within fair use.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Easy in-browser editing with subtitles, translation, lip sync and stock. For developer-creators, OpenEdit is free and agent-native.

headline_features.detail: No GUI and no timeline: a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) composes the edit in HTML and CSS, and VEED Engine renders it locally (VEED says up to 2.2x faster than Chrome-based renderers). It can caption, reframe, add motion graphics, turn slides or sites into video and generate media for credits. Apple Silicon on macOS 26 only. Pipeline Apache-2.0; renderer binaries closed (PolyForm Shield).

headline_features.feature: VEED MCP server, ChatGPT app, Make.com
headline_features.detail: Connects AI assistants and agents so they can create and edit video (Apr 30). Takes a prompt to a finished video inside ChatGPT (May 5). Make.com scenarios (May 7).
Re-dubs a video with your own audio and more natural mouth movement, in Full HD, for videos up to an hour.
Animated caption presets: Handwritten, Whisper, Fusion (Feb 23). Programmatic subtitles in 100+ languages (May 18).

headline_features.feature: GenAI Studio: Kling 3.0 and Multi-Shot; Epidemic Sound
headline_features.detail: Generation from text or images with Kling 3.0 (Feb 6). One prompt to a sequence of camera angles (Apr 23). Epidemic Sound music and sound effects inside the editor (May 6).

tools.name: Kapwing
tools.positioning: A browser editor for teams that has re-centred on Kai, an AI agent that plans and edits and models other vendors' generators, plus an MCP server. Pricing: freemium (4-minute free exports, 50 AI credits), then a subscription with AI credits; MCP at no extra cost.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: A collaborative web editor with strong subtitles, translation and dubbing, an agent that shows the cost before it acts, and no install.

headline_features.detail: A task checklist with progress shown on the canvas. You approve the estimated credit cost first and can interrupt with a refund. Kai checks its own output and corrects errors, states its limits, and reads uploads (waveform peaks, transcripts) before planning. Faceswaps of real people are refused.

headline_features.feature: Multimodal moment finding and speaker smart crop
headline_features.detail: Kai assembles clips from visual and audio cues (example: 'Find the dunks from the third quarter') and keeps a speaker in frame. The agent's plan shows cost, prompts and models before you confirm, and plans under 40 credits are accepted automatically.
12 new presets (Editorial, Scribble, Zing). Line length follows the aspect ratio: short and bold for vertical, longer for landscape. New animations: Growing, Vibrate, Typing and Word Fly.

1.0 for all users on Oct 12 and 1.1 on Oct 27. Tools upload, create projects, export, caption, transcribe, translate, dub, generate images and video, and edit through the transcript or by placing layers in natural language. Each MCP project opens as an editable Kai chat.
AI blur of moving objects from a text prompt, such as 'blur faces' or 'blur license plates'.

tools.name: Canva (video editor, Magic Video, Canva AI 2.0)
tools.positioning: Design-first, template-and-brand-kit video for marketers and social teams, inside the tool they already use for graphics. Pricing: free, then Canva Pro or Teams subscriptions, with monthly AI usage limits on premium AI.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Brand kits, huge template libraries and team workflows. Video is 'good enough' for social and sits next to every other asset. Weak on precise editing; one review notes no chroma key.

headline_features.detail: Upload footage and describe the result; it assembles a social-ready edit of up to 60 s with cuts, synced audio and transitions. On all plans, including free, with an hourly limit; cropping may miss the subject.
headline_features.as_of: 2026-11-01 (help page returned 403 to the fetcher; details are from the search snippet)

headline_features.detail: Text-to-video clips with synced sound on Google's Veo 3, for paid plans.

Conversational design, iterative agentic editing, layered object intelligence and 'living memory'. Third-party coverage of Canva Create also names Magic Video 2.0, AI video effects and caption styles.

tools.name: Edits (Meta / Instagram)
tools.positioning: A free platform-owned mobile editor (launched Apr 2025) that competes with CapCut. Desktop version announced. Pricing: free, no watermark; more AI assistant usage through a Meta One subscription.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Free, no watermark, made for Reels, and tied to Instagram data: an assistant that reads your own Reels performance, weekly ideas from past Reels, and links to IG accounts and Reels.

headline_features.detail: Reads your follows, views, retention, likes, shares, comments and Instagram trends; suggests audio and concepts that performed. Meta positions it as an analyst: 'the creative calls are still yours'. Free with a usage cap; Meta One for more.
Previewed with project sync between phone and desktop; 'coming soon', operating systems not stated.
Clickable IG account and Reel links in exports, 25 video effects, 10 weekly content ideas from past Reels, and multiple takes on the storyboard.

headline_features.feature: Free AI translation with lip sync on Instagram
headline_features.detail: Dubs the creator's voice and matches the lips, free for public accounts, in 14 languages after the July 2026 expansion (Japanese, Korean, French, German, Italian). Platform-side, not inside Edits.

tools.name: YouTube Create / Shorts editor / YouTube Studio
tools.positioning: Free editing and AI built into the platform. Pricing: free.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Free, publishes straight to YouTube, and auto-dubbing and A/B tests run where the audience is.

headline_features.detail: Chat-driven editing for Shorts and the Create app: picks the best takes, adds music and transitions, inserts text, removes pauses, and moves to the manual timeline when you want. YouTube's words: 'edits with you, not for you'.
Opened to all creators in 27 languages (Feb 2026), with Expressive Speech in 8 languages. Lip sync is still a pilot with select channels. Real-time dubbing for live streams is in testing.

headline_features.feature: Studio: video A/B tests, three thumbnails, Ask Studio
headline_features.detail: Test different edits; up to three thumbnails per video; an AI that drafts brand pitches.

headline_features.feature: Edit with AI (first-draft Shorts from the camera roll)
